inputs.wacc_rationale: Equity model, so a cost of equity in RMB, not a WACC. China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta 1.6 x ERP 6.0% = 11.4% market-implied, plus ~1pp for B3/B+ credit, governance (Jan/Feb 2026 connected transactions) and nil-distribution risk = 12.5% base. Bull 11.5% (rating path to B1/BB-, REIT recycling proven), bear 14.5% (distressed-equity rate). The 11.8-11.88% coupons on 2025-26 offshore notes bound the equity rate from below.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities RMB3,117m (ROU assets RMB862m) stay inside book equity; no separate deduction. Immaterial against RMB123.9bn of investment property.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI RMB34,883m (42.3% of total equity) is treated PRO-RATA: every balance-sheet haircut is multiplied by the attributable fraction k = 47,658 / 82,542 = 0.5774 before it hits attributable NAV. The NCI is overwhelmingly the 32.8% A-share float of Seazen Holdings (601155.SS, which owns essentially all operating assets) plus project-level minorities inside it, so it shares losses in proportion. Deducting NCI at book against a sub-book valuation would be wrong by ~RMB15-20bn.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md. Seazen straddles three rows: an IAS-40 mall landlord (181 Wuyue Plazas, RMB123.9bn at fair value, ~RMB13bn/yr commercial revenue), an inventory-heavy residential developer in run-off (RMB64.8bn of stock for sale, contracted sales RMB6.4bn in H1 FY2026 vs RMB169.5bn-era peak), and a distressed capital structure (Moody's B3, 11.8-11.88% offshore coupons, going-concern paragraph in the FY2025 audit note (iii)). The parts cannot be valued separately and summed because RMB49.5bn of RMB55.4bn borrowings is secured across both the malls and the inventory and the NCI is pro-rata across everything, so the model is the developer row -- haircut NTA x exit P/NAV blended with normalised earnings x exit P/E -- with the distressed row supplying the bear case and the REIT row supplying the mall cap-rate cross-check. NOT an owner-FCF DCF: operating cash flow was negative in FY2024, FY2025 and H1 FY2026 (owner FCF FY2025 -RMB2.3bn after RMB3.5bn cash interest), so there is no owner flow to discount; the engine route would also deduct NCI at book against a valuation below book. MECHANICS. Attributable NAV today = book equity attributable (47,658) + k x scenario haircuts on inventory, receivables, JV/associates, DTA, investment properties and off-BS mortgage guarantees. NAV accretes by attributable NPAT for 5 years (nil dividends). Year-5 value per share = 70% x NAV5 x exit P/NAV + 30% x EPS5 x exit P/E, discounted at the scenario cost of equity. No perpetuity. DASHBOARD. assumptions[scenario] are NAV-model parameters, not engine component paths; the slider engine cannot re-derive these values and the dashboard should display the stored ones (same situation as AFI.NZ / SUM.NZ). FIRST VALUATION of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF): fresh build, no reconciliation block.

historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less interest income) is negative in FY2024 (-4,654), FY2025 (-2,294) and H1 FY2026 (-937); a CAGR on a sign-changing series is undefined. FY2021 owner FCF was -355 after interest income, so even the 5-year endpoints are negative.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case haircut-NAV accretion from retained earnings (normalised ROE ~2.3% on adjusted NAV, no dividends); historical CAGRs are a collapse, not a trend to extrapolate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR +1.3% vs revenue 3yr CAGR -23.0% and EPS 5yr CAGR -48.5%: book equity has been held flat by retained mall income and nil dividends while development revenue fell ~70% from the FY2021 peak. Book value is NOT corroborated by earnings or cash flow, which is why every scenario haircuts it.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are negative (FY2021 169.5bn -> FY2025 53.1bn). EPS 3yr CAGR is +14.5% only because FY2022 EPS was 0.04 (near zero). No SBC in any year (sbc_source: cash flow statements FY2023-H1 FY2026 show nil; FY2018-22 immaterial).

probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, band collapsed.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35% / base 45% / bull 20%, against the house default 15/50/35. Bear carries roughly the 5-year cumulative default/impairment probability of a B3-rated issuer (~30-35%): offshore notes still price at 11.8-11.88%, OCF has been negative for 2.5 years, RMB10.8bn of borrowings fall due within 12 months against RMB7.85bn of cash (RMB2.3bn restricted), the FY2025 audit carries a going-concern emphasis, and January/February 2026 connected-party transactions show the controlling family will transact with the company on its own terms. Bull is capped at 20% because it needs three things to go right at once (sector bottom, REIT recycling at book across the portfolio, refinancing in single digits), and even then the bull IV only reaches the A-share look-through at a 30% discount.

scenario_narratives.bear: Survives but the book is impaired (not liquidation, which leaves equity nil). National new-home sales keep falling into 2027; the RMB64.8bn inventory is cleared at 25% below carrying value, 35% of the RMB31.4bn receivables (largely JV/related-party) are irrecoverable, JV/associate interests are written down 40%, the RMB5.8bn deferred tax asset is derecognised, mall values fall 10% on cap-rate expansion in competed lower-tier submarkets, and 10% of the RMB11.2bn purchaser-mortgage guarantees are called. Attributable NAV falls from RMB6.56 to RMB2.24/share. Earnings are nil in year 1 as impairments absorb the mall profit, recovering to RMB300m by year 5. The offshore notes are refinanced at 11-12% or extended; a further discounted placement to the controlling family is likely. Exit at 0.15x NAV and 6x earnings, discounted at 14.5%.
scenario_narratives.base: Controlled run-off of development funded by the malls. Inventory clears 10% below book, 15% of receivables are lost, JV/associates are haircut 20%, half the DTA never crystallises; malls hold book value, corroborated by the Commercial REIT (RMB1.5bn for two plazas = book average) and an implied ~6.3% cap rate. Attributable NAV RMB5.11/share. Attributable NPAT RMB850m in FY2026E (consensus-implied ~RMB810m from the 10.95x forward P/E; H1 FY2026 was RMB608m with the seasonal H2 impairment pattern of FY2025 repeating more mildly), growing 5% a year as the 11.88% notes are refinanced cheaper and commercial income grows 2-4%. No dividend inside 5 years. Exit at 0.45x haircut NAV (Longfor's ~0.3x reported book, adjusted for an already-written-down NAV with 60%+ of the asset base in income-producing malls) blended 70/30 with 9x earnings, discounted at 12.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Sector bottoms in 2027 and the REIT template recycles the mall portfolio at book. Inventory clears at a 5% discount, receivables lose 10%, JV/associates 10%, DTA 25%. The Moody's/S&P path continues to B1/BB-, offshore refinancing drops to high single digits, saving ~RMB300m/yr of interest; construction-management (5.5m sqm signed in H1 FY2026) adds asset-light fees. Attributable NPAT RMB1.3bn in FY2026E growing 8%; NAV reaches RMB6.83/share by year 5. Exit re-rates to 0.60x NAV (toward SOE landlords and the A-share's own multiple) and 12x earnings, at 11.5%. Dividends could resume by year 4-5 but are excluded; including a 20% payout would add roughly HK$0.05.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Seazen is an asset-backed survivor whose equity value is set by what the book is really worth and what multiple a going-concern private Chinese developer earns on it -- not by cash flow, which is negative, and not by the A-share price, which is onshore liquidity. The malls are the only part of the book that an outside price (the approved REIT) corroborates; everything else is haircut. At HK$1.43 the stock is at base value and ~15% above the probability-weighted value, so there is no margin of safety for the 35% impairment case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Refinancing: RMB10.8bn due within 12 months vs RMB5.5bn free cash; any loss of offshore/onshore market access forces asset sales below book or a restructuring
Inventory and receivable realisation below the base haircuts if national sales fall further in 2027
Mall cap-rate expansion: a 10% IP revaluation is RMB12.4bn at 100%, RMB7.2bn attributable (RMB0.99/share)
Controlling-family dilution: a second discounted placement like February 2026's at HK$2.39 would now be below HK$1.50
Exit multiple: the single biggest lever (sensitivity grid); HK-listed private developers have not re-rated above 0.3x book since 2021
FX: 1030.HK is an HKD quote on RMB assets; a 5% RMB depreciation takes 5% off every HKD value here and raises the RMB cost of the USD notes

a_share_look_through.non_a_share_note: Segment table H1 FY2026: non-A-share assets 10,524 (mostly intercompany loans and the eliminated associate interest) less liabilities 3,647 (offshore senior notes net of the A-share's own). Taken at 50% here.
a_share_look_through.read: 1030.HK trades at a ~60% discount to its A-share look-through. That is the usual A/H developer gap (Vanke H trades 30-40% below the A) plus the holdco's 11.8-11.88% offshore notes and the February 2026 connected placement. The A-share price is not used as an anchor -- it is an onshore-liquidity price, not an asset value -- but it confirms the NAV is not the binding constraint on value; the exit multiple is.

mall_portfolio_cap_rate.reit_parity: Approved Commercial REIT: ~RMB1.5bn for two Wuyue Plazas vs RMB123.9bn / 181 completed malls = RMB0.68bn average. REIT pricing roughly equals book, so the IAS-40 carrying value is held at 0% haircut in base and bull; bear takes 10% for cap-rate expansion in competed lower-tier submarkets (H1 FY2026 fair-value loss RMB203m).

liquidation_waterfall.note: Distressed-row check (not a scenario): IP at 70%, inventory 60%, receivables 50%, JV/associates 50%, cash 100%, DTA/PPE nil = ~RMB161bn of realisable assets against RMB176bn of liabilities. A forced liquidation leaves nil for equity. The bear scenario is therefore a going-concern survivor with an impaired book and a 0.15x exit, not a liquidation; the weight on bear (35%) is the probability-of-impairment proxy for a B3/B+ issuer.

peer_p_book.note: HK-listed survivors: Longfor (0960.HK, closest comp: mall landlord + developer, no default) ~0.25-0.30x reported book; Vanke H ~0.2x; SOE landlords (CR Land, COLI) ~0.5-0.6x. Seazen at HK$1.43 = 0.19x reported book, 0.25x base adjusted NAV. Base IV at 0.19x book / 0.25x adjusted NAV sits on Longfor's multiple after allowing for Seazen's higher funding cost.
